Policy & Claims Copilot – Knowledge Base
Document
1. Overview
The Policy & Claims Copilot  is designed to assist customers, insurance agents, and claims teams by
providing accurate, consistent, and real-time information about insurance policies and claims processes. This system leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer
queries and perform preliminary claim validations. 2.

Policy Coverage
2.1 What is Covered
Coverage varies by policy type but typically includes:
Hospitalization expenses (room rent, ICU, nursing)
Pre- and post-hospitalization costs (e.g., consultations, diagnostics)
Daycare procedures not requiring 24-hour admission
Emergency ambulance services
Certain critical illnesses (as specified in policy documents)
Maternity benefits (if included)
2.2 What is Not Covered
Common exclusions include:
Pre-existing diseases (during waiting period)
Cosmetic or aesthetic treatments
Self-inflicted injuries or suicide attempts
Injuries due to intoxication or substance abuse
Experimental or unproven treatments
Non-prescribed treatments or therapies
3.

Limits and Sub-Limits
Policies may include financial caps such as:
Room Rent Limit : e.g., 1% of sum insured per day
ICU Charges Limit : e.g., 2% of sum insured per day
Specific Treatment Caps : Fixed limits for procedures like cataract surgery•

Maternity Limit : Maximum payable amount for childbirth expenses
Co-payment Clause : Percentage of claim paid by policyholder (e.g., 10–20%)
4.

Waiting Periods
Waiting periods are durations during which certain claims are not admissible:
Initial Waiting Period : Typically 30 days from policy start (except accidents)
Pre-existing Disease Waiting Period : Usually 2–4 years
Specific Illness Waiting Period : e.g., hernia, cataract (1–2 years)
Maternity Waiting Period : Typically 9 months to 2 years
5.

Claim Submission Process
5.1 Steps to File a Claim
Notify insurer or TPA (Third Party Administrator)
Submit claim form (online or offline)
Provide required documents
Undergo claim assessment
Receive approval/rejection decision
5.2 Types of Claims
Cashless Claims : Direct settlement with network hospital
Reimbursement Claims : Policyholder pays upfront and claims later
6.

Claim Timelines
Claim intimation: Within 24–48 hours of hospitalization
Document submission: Within 7–15 days after discharge
Claim processing: Typically 15–30 working days
Reimbursement settlement: Within 7–10 days after approval
7. Required Documents
Typical documents include:
Duly filled claim form
Hospital bills and receipts
Discharge summary•

8. Claim Pre-Check Logic
The system performs a preliminary validation before claim submission:
8.1 Eligibility Check
Is the policy active? Is the condition covered? Has the waiting period been completed? 8.2 Financial Check
Does the claim exceed policy limits? Are sub-limits applicable? Is co-payment required?

8.3 Documentation Check
Are all required documents available? Are documents valid and complete? 9.

Example Claim Scenarios
Scenario 1: Covered Claim
Condition: Appendicitis
Policy active: Yes
Waiting period: Completed
Outcome: Likely approved
Scenario 2: Not Covered
Condition: Cosmetic surgery
Outcome: Rejected (excluded treatment)
Scenario 3: Partial Approval
Condition: Cataract surgery
Sub-limit applies
Outcome: Approved with capped payout•

10. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Q1: Can I claim immediately after buying a policy?

A: Only for accidents; other claims are subject to waiting periods. Q2: What happens if documents are missing? A: Claims may be delayed or rejected. Q3: Can I use any hospital? A: Yes, but cashless claims are only available at network hospitals. Q4: How long does claim approval take? A: Typically 15–30 working days. 11. System Usage Guidelines for RAG
Store this document in vector database as chunks (200–500 tokens)
Tag sections (coverage, exclusions, claims, documents, etc.)

Use semantic search for retrieval
Combine retrieved context with LLM for response generation
Ensure responses cite relevant sections
12. Disclaimer
This document is for informational purposes only. Final claim decisions are subject to policy terms, insurer
evaluation, and regulatory guidelines. End of Document•
